text:
olivia.sre: Heads-up: we're pushing an SLO update for the embeddings batch service tomorrow 2024-11-02 05:00-05:20 UTC. Change: p95 latency target will move from 300ms -> 450ms for the next 24h as we run an optimization that trades latency for lower token-cost on backfilled jobs. Internal RFC: https://go/internal/embeddings-slo-update
ben.prod: What triggers this change? Customer-facing notice required?
olivia.sre: Trigger: cost spike in batch backfills combined with memory pressure on large-pool nodes. No customer-visible API change for real-time embeddings. We'll add a short note in infra-status and only notify customers running scheduled bulk backfills if they exceed quota thresholds.
hao.ml: Quick context: the optimization applies to the batch pipeline only. We enable a new merge-window and chunk-size heuristic that reduces memory churn but increases tail latency on very large inputs. Measured quality impact: none, cost win ~23% on 10k-job sample.
ravi.oncall: Canary plan? Who's watching metrics?
olivia.sre: Canary: enable on shadow batch pool at 04:50 UTC for 10m, then ramp to 20% of backfill jobs at 05:00 for 10m if green. Watchers: @ravi.oncall and @hao.ml. Dashboards: embeddings-batch/p95, batch-job-error-rate/5m, node-mem-pressure.
ci-bot: Canary toggle created -> job=canary-emb-batch-20241102, pools=[shadow-batch,canary-batch-1]
ben.prod: Are there any Dedicated/Private tenant implications? Some customers run large offline jobs on Dedicated.
olivia.sre: Dedicated tenants with reserved batch pools are unaffected unless they opt into the new heuristic. We'll not enable it on reserved pools; only on shared infra. Private on-prem customers: no change.
hao.ml: Rollback criteria: if batch-job-error-rate > 0.8% above baseline for >4m OR node-mem-pressure > 75% for >3m -> rollback to old heuristic and abort rollout. Manual cancel: `#/jobs cancel canary-emb-batch-20241102`
alerts-bot: Monitoring suppression scheduled -> embeddings-batch SLO alerts muted 05:00-05:30 UTC (announced in suppression channel).
ben.prod: Excluding scheduled perf/load tests? There's a throughput run at 05:05 in us-east that could pollute results.
olivia.sre: Yes, please tag those runs with `traffic-tag: perf` or set header `x-debug=true`. Any job with `x-debug=true` will be ignored by canary metrics.
ravi.oncall: Runbook excerpt pasted below:
```
# Embeddings batch SLO change runbook (excerpt)
T-30m: confirm canary pool healthy and backup config available
T-10m: enable canary on shadow pool (04:50) -> observe embeddings-batch/p95 and batch-job-error-rate
05:00: ramp to 20% backfill jobs -> monitor node-mem-pressure and error-rate
If error-rate >0.8% above baseline for >4m OR mem >75% for >3m -> rollback: `job rollback canary-emb-batch-20241102`
If transient p95 spikes but error-rate stable -> continue and escalate to ML team for sample inspection
Post: revert monitoring suppression and add postmortem notes with traces from sampled jobs
```
hao.ml: We'll also capture sample inputs and outputs for 1000 jobs during the canary for QA comparison. 
ben.prod: Sounds good. I'll coordinate messaging for platform teams and add an entry to the maintenance calendar.
olivia.sre: TL;DR: SLO p95 for embeddings-batch relaxed for 24h starting 05:00 UTC tomorrow, canary at 04:50, exclusion for perf runs via `x-debug=true`, rollback thresholds defined. Ping this thread to join the bridge.
ravi.oncall: ack :white_check_mark: I'll be on watch and will post in #alerts if we need to abort.
